correctness.rationale: RESULT.md lines 5–30 and 32–88. Since t is not in F5, none of t=±2 or t=−1 can hold. One nonzero coordinate gives a nonzero derivative; with exactly two, the partials give a square-coordinate system of determinant 4−t²; with three, its determinant is (2−t)²(2+2t). Thus the projective gradient has no common zero over the algebraic closure. Bézout then excludes reducibility of the smooth plane quartic and gives the four-point line bound; adjunction gives genus three. Independently enumerated all 651 points and all 651 dual lines in a last-nonzero-coordinate normalization, with pair-valued field arithmetic. This gave 56 points and the spectrum (63,168,196,0,224), and converting only for comparison to the given certificate's index order recovered all four entries of each displayed line block and a disjoint cover of 0 through 55. No smaller cover is possible. The count attains 26+2·3·5. Tafazolian's Theorem 1.1(ii) identifies the unique F25-maximal genus-three isomorphism class with the Klein quartic's S4-model. In addition, independent computation obtained transitivity explicitly: signed permutations have point orbit sizes 8,24,24; adjoining the projective matrix with rows (2u,2u,3+u), (3u,3u,3+u), (3+4u,2+u,0) acts transitively and preserves all 56 points. Its image curve is the same curve by Bézout (56>4·4). Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_quartic_check.py. The bundled script was read, not executed. This is a finite exhaustive verification and explicit certificate, not a claim at other fields or about all minimum covers.
